NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The proposed intervention is to prevent chain lubricant carbonisation by retuning the lubrication dose interval and duty cycle to operate only during cooler chain segments. Standard practice applies continuous lubrication at a fixed dose regardless of temperature. This mitigation departs by scheduling lubrication pulses to coincide with the chain's coolest position in the cycle, directly reducing the cumulative thermal stress on the oil. The closest existing practice is fixed-interval lubrication; this is different because it uses temperature-driven scheduling to minimise residence time at high temperature. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by reducing the time the lubricant is exposed to peak temperatures above its flash point.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the Arrhenius equation for oxidation rate: k = A * exp(-Ea/RT), where k is the reaction rate, Ea is activation energy, R is the gas constant, and T is temperature in Kelvin. At 210°C (483 K), the oxidation rate is significantly higher than at lower temperatures. By scheduling lubrication to occur only when the chain is below 150°C (423 K), the exposure time at high temperature is reduced. For a typical mineral oil with Ea ≈ 50 kJ/mol, the oxidation rate at 423 K is ~1/5 of that at 483 K. A 70% reduction in high-temperature exposure time reduces the cumulative oxidation by ~60%, directly mitigating carbonisation.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- (c) Retune lubrication dose interval from continuous to 30-second pulses every 5 minutes
- (c) Retune lubrication duty cycle to 100% output during cool zone (chain position 180-270°), 0% during hot zone (0-180°)
- (c) Set lubrication system trigger to chain position sensor (existing equipment)
- (c) Adjust lubrication dose volume from 2 ml/min to 4 ml/pulse (total volume unchanged)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installation: 0 rows added (all parameter changes use existing equipment)
- Operation: Same operator workload (no additional monitoring; existing position sensor used)
- Maintenance: Same maintenance interval (same lubricant volume, same system components)
- Operational loss: Zero (lubrication occurs during normal machine operation; no production downtime)
- Cost class: Same (no new hardware; only parameter retuning)

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run two identical stenter chains for 1000 operating hours each, one with standard continuous lubrication and one with the new pulsed-cool-zone schedule. Measure carbonisation buildup weekly using FTIR spectroscopy on lubricant samples drawn from the chain pins.
Instruments: FTIR spectrometer, temperature sensors (existing), lubricant sampling kit.
Pass/fail threshold: <20% increase in carbonaceous compounds (measured as absorbance at 1600 cm⁻¹) in the pulsed-lubrication chain vs >40% in continuous.
Duration: 1000 hours (one typical maintenance cycle).
Kill criterion: Any tracking fault or edge marking observed during the test.
